subtitle: CSV, JSON, and Excel — three readers, one DataFrame habit.

code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv", parse_dates=["order_date"])
print(df.dtypes["order_date"])
print(df.head(3)[["order_id", "order_date"]])

# datetime64[ns]
#    order_id order_date
# 0      1001 2026-01-03
# 1      1002 2026-01-04
# 2      1003 2026-01-05
caption: Without parse_dates, order_date comes back as object — plain strings, useless for real date math.

eyebrow: Why it matters: filtering by real dates
caption: Pandas compares the string correctly against the column only because order_date is a real datetime64[ns] type now.

eyebrow: pd.read_json() — reading Lesson 15's export back in
caption: Lesson 15's JSON stored quantity as a quoted string, but read_json infers the real numeric type anyway.

eyebrow: pd.read_excel() — the syntax, for when you need it
caption: Needs openpyxl installed. sheet_name picks the sheet by name or index; everything else works the same once the DataFrame exists.
